where: crates/dla-cli/tests/alloc_test_jvm.rs:447-476 (the row at docs/VERIFY.md:509 calls these assertions "true on every build")
text: The new warm-up assertions depend on how much CPU the JVM gets, so they can fail with the warm-up working. The test itself passed in all 8 whole-binary runs here (4 on JDK 21, 4 on JDK 25). I replayed its measurement with the same dla commands (idle driver, 20 checkpoints, DLA_WARM_ROUNDS=0 against the default) and applied the test's assertions to each cold/warm pair. Quiet machine: 12 of 12 pairs pass. Four harness runs at once, which is what the test binary's own threads do on a 4-core runner: 2 of 24 pairs fail. On JDK 21 the cold first step was 36 KB, under the 50 KB line at line 472; on JDK 25 the warm run started at 9.84 MB, below the cold run's 10.51 MB, failing line 448. Four busy loops: 2 of 5 pairs fail on JDK 21 (cold first step 32 KB; first-step ratio 0.77 against the 0.7 line). The warm-up stops after 3 s (harness/jvm/DlaDump.java:179), so a loaded machine warms less and the start value and first step move. Two relations held in all 41 Linux pairs, loaded ones included: the early rise (point 1 to 15) warm under 0.75 of cold (largest 0.69), and the rise from the first reading (point 0 to 15) warm at most 0.58 of cold. The second also holds in both macOS logs (0.66 and 0.74), and two cold runs against each other gave 0.72 to 1.38. Direction: assert one relation on the rise from the first reading (for example warm under 0.85 of cold) in place of the start value and first-step checks, or measure a second time before failing. Then correct the row's "true on every build".

The 500 KB line switches the early-rise comparison off on Linux with JDK 25, the default JDK of the Ubuntu runner, although the relation holds there. The cold rise was 355 to 472 KB in all 22 JDK 25 runs I measured, so the comparison never ran. Warm was under 0.75 of cold in all 18 JDK 25 pairs (largest 0.69, so the margin is thin). On JDK 21 it is also skipped at times (cold rises of 474 and 499 KB seen), which the row's "JDK 21 on Linux" does not say. Only macOS needed the comparison dropped (cold rise about 340 KB, warm the same).

The measured figures are not what a rerun shows. The row says the first-step ratio was "0.17 to 0.4 with the warm-up and 0.8 to 1.0 without it". I measured 0.08 to 0.53 in quiet pairs, 0.25 to 0.42 in the whole-binary runs and up to 0.69 with four harness runs at once. Without the warm-up, two cold runs against each other gave 0.54 to 1.85 on JDK 21, so the 0.7 line lies inside that range. The test still fails without the warm-up in 29 of 30 cold-against-cold pairs on each JDK, because the start value and rise checks catch what the first step lets through. The test comment says the warm first step was "at most a third" of the cold one; the fixer's own run measured 0.41. The row also gives the JDK 25 cold rise as about 0.35 MB; I saw 0.36 to 0.47 MB.

where: harness/jvm/DlaDump.java:676-677 (isTestLocation, the whole-location fallback; it runs before the package check at line 642)
text: A project spelled through a link is still read as test output when a directory above it is named like one. When the location is under the project only after links are resolved, the whole location is checked for test parts, not only the part below the project. Run by hand with the new agent: real path .../ws/java/test/proj, DLA_PROJECT given by a link to it, classes loaded by the JVM's own loader: coverage project=0, also with DLA_PROJECT_PACKAGES=zz.shop; with the real root it is 2. The same happens for a location spelled through a link named out/test against a real root. The old agent gives the same result, so this is not a regression, and dla harness run with the JVM's own loader does not reach it (both sides are canonical). It is a remaining case of the same defect, and no test covers it. Direction: when the names differ, relativize the written location against the resolved root and the resolved location against the written root, and drop the whole-location check for a location that is under the project by resolution.

The list misses the flight recorder's fourth thread, `JFR Recording Scheduler`. A timed recording starts it, and `dla attach` starts exactly such a recording (`JFR.start ... duration=Ns`, /home/user/dla/crates/dla-sample/src/attach/jcmd.rs:487-490). I took real dumps on JDK 21.0.12 and JDK 25.0.5 before, during and after `JFR.start name=.. settings=profile duration=4s filename=..`: 7 threads before, 10 after, and the Scheduler thread stays after the recording ends and after `JFR.stop`. With the fixed binary `dla summarize non-heap` on those dumps still reports `metric:threads/total` 7 -> 8 and `group:thread/name:JFR Recording Scheduler` d=1; with the recording started between dump 2 and 3 `dla trend` reads the total as `stair` (rise 1.25). So a thread series that spans DLA's own attach recording still moves by the recorder, which is what the constant's comment and the limitation line say does not happen. It is not the jvm-audit-window failure (the harness capture uses no duration). Suggested: add the name to the list, to the unit test and to the limitation line.
